title: Nine
events_chronological: As a boy at a Catholic school, Guido Contini sneaks down to the beach to watch the prostitute Saraghina dance, and is beaten for it by the priests.
Guido's mother watches over him from the edge of every memory, and he loses her early.
Guido becomes Italy's most celebrated director, with a run of hits and a public that hangs on his every word.
Guido marries the actress Luisa, who gives up her own career for him.
Guido takes a mistress, Carla, and installs her in hotels near wherever he happens to be shooting.
Guido's last two films fail, and he finds he cannot write the next one.
A Rome press conference for the unwritten "Italia" turns into an ambush, and Guido flees to a spa at Anzio.
His costume designer and confidante Lilli tells him plainly that he has nothing to say.
Carla follows him to the spa, checks into his hotel and stages an elaborate seduction.
Guido summons his muse, the star Claudia, and cannot tell her what the part is.
The producer starts building sets for a film that has no script, and the crew waits on the lot.
Luisa arrives at the spa and sees Carla's name in the hotel register.
Told to leave, Carla takes an overdose in her room and survives it.
Guido imagines every woman in his life singing for him at once on an empty soundstage.
Luisa confronts Guido in front of the press and tells him she is done being his material.
Guido abandons the film on the day shooting was to start, and the sets are struck.
Guido spends two years in silence, until Lilli talks him into trying once more.
Guido calls Luisa to a screen test for a film about the two of them, and she agrees to sit and watch.
syuzhet_notes: The film's present is the fortnight before a shoot that never starts, and it keeps breaking into two kinds of interruption: memories - told-order bullets 5, 7, 8, 10 and 12 - and staged musical numbers that happen only inside Guido's head. The largest of those is told-order bullet 1, which opens the film on a soundstage that exists nowhere in the story.
fabula_notes: Several numbers are fantasy rather than event and have no fixed position in time; they are placed here at the moment in Guido's life they draw on. His childhood, his mother's death and the arc of his career are recalled rather than staged as present action.
